key_insight: Oxide-cap size and position alter aluminum-particle combustion: front caps enhance local evaporation near the cap–metal junction, while rear caps absorb heat and lower reaction temperatures.
engineering_relevance: Cap-aware evaporation and drag models can improve Lagrangian predictions of burning aluminum particles without resolving each particle’s boundary layer.
method: Boundary-layer-resolved simulations varying cap size, cap orientation, and particle Reynolds number.
Film-state modeling with a 0.55-rule for temperature, species mass fractions, and pressure.
Optimized Whitaker and Schiller–Naumann correlations, extended to oxide-capped doublet particles.
evidence_signal: The revised evaporation and drag correlations agree well with the simulations; exposed aluminum area supports rear-cap evaporation predictions, while front caps require an additional flux correction.
watch_item: Front-cap evaporation needs particular care at high particle Reynolds numbers; validation beyond the simulated conditions is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Influence of an oxide cap on the combustion of aluminum particles using boundary-layer resolved simulations
